name: NQ Playbook
tagline: What the NQ setups that funded traders actually use look like once 16 years of minute data grade them — the opening range, EMA pullbacks, liquidity sweeps and VWAP, plus the contract math that fits inside a $2,000 drawdown.
summary: NQ is the prop-firm default because its dollar swing makes $200–600 days reachable with one contract — and because the same volatility quietly decides which setups survive a trailing floor. The measured picture: raw breakout touches fail ~60% of the time and only confirmation-close variants with structural stops pay; the taught liquidity-sweep models carry real information but measured negative expectancy after costs; VWAP fades win often enough to look safe and lose rarely enough to be fatal on a ratcheting floor. This guide ranks the setup menu by evidence class, maps the session clock (the market wakes before 9:30 and the second-biggest minute is 15:50), and reduces sizing to arithmetic: on a 50K account the honest unit is 1–2 MNQ, because one NQ with a normal 30-point stop already spends 30% of the drawdown.
oneLiner: Trade confirmation closes at structural stops, size in MNQ against the floor rather than the balance, and let the 9:25–10:30 window carry the day.
keyQuote: On the initial break you're volunteering to be that liquidity. Enter on the retest, not the break.

stats.label: First breaks of the 15-min range that fail

lead: Every claim below carries its evidence class — measured, vendor, or folklore — so the setup menu can be trusted at the size it deserves.
highlights: Touch entries lose, close entries survive — the one finding every source class agrees on.
The sweep moment carries information; the taught sweep SYSTEM does not — measured −0.1 to −0.2R per trade after costs.
Fade-style 65% win rates come with profit factors near 1.1 — a fat-tail loser erases weeks of a trailing floor.
NQ wakes around 9:05 AM; a stop sized for the calm pre-open chart is undersized for the open by 2–3×.
One NQ at a 30-point stop risks 30% of a $2,000 drawdown — micros are the default eval unit, not the cautious one.
One hero day is a tax: consistency rules convert your best session into a higher target.

articles.title: Is the opening range breakout profitable on NQ? (2,159-day test)
articles.takeaway: 16-yr 1-min test: ~60% of first breaks fail; far-side-stop ORB deeply negative; only midpoint-stop/close-all variant positive, 1-in-4 hit rate, 18-loss streaks.

articles.title: Do liquidity sweeps work? (measured)
articles.takeaway: Sweep setups beat random controls (real information) but taught models measure 47–48% WR, negative R/trade; viral sweep pass-rate 18.3% vs coin-flip 35.3%.

articles.title: The best time of day to trade ES and NQ (measured)
articles.takeaway: NQ activity triples from 9:25; 9:30 = 3.25× median minute; 15:50 MOC second spike; no consistently directional 15-min slot in 16 years.

articles.takeaway: 65% win rate, PF ~1.15 pre-costs on 15-min; 5-min variant negative after costs — the fade's fat tail eats the ratchet.
